wording: P100 adapts Reed's Self-Transcendence Scale to Spanish: 19 experts gave a global content validity coefficient S-CVI of 0.92; in 116 adults internal consistency was alpha 0.772 (test) and 0.833 (retest); scores correlated with psychological well-being (r 0.636) and spiritual well-being (0.687); the abstract reports three factors explaining 42.3% of the variance and the four- and three-factor models fit acceptably (RMSEA 0.053 and 0.049).
locator: P100 Objectives to Conclusion, Tables 1-3 (read in full)
counterevidence_limits: Small online sample; intraclass ICC 0.278 (p 0.097) is low. Slips: Bartlett 'df = 1,050' (105 for 15 items); three factors 42.3% vs four factors 41.4% elsewhere; one-factor SRMR printed 0.837; the 'no children' row total is 16 (11 + 50 = 61); Pc values for three items do not follow the stated formula (TR0-APP-02).
operationalization: APP Transcendence = self-transcendence measured in nursing research
verification_phrases: P100|global content validity coefficient (S-CVI) = 0.92 || P100|df = 1,050 || P100|three factors explained 42.3% of the variance
change_vs_prev_cycle: carried from TRA-APP-01 unchanged (not re-read in TRB)

wording: P100's I-CVIs equal the share of agreeing experts (18/19, 17/19, 16/19, 15/18), its modified kappas follow from its printed I-CVI and Pc, S-CVI is 0.922, and RMSEA (0.053, 0.050, 0.053, 0.078) and chi-square p (0.024, 0.039, 0.023, < 0.001) reproduce for the four factor models. Two pre-registered checks were not supported: the chance agreement Pc = C(N, A) 0.5^N gives 0.00033, 0.0018 and 0.0031 for 17/19, 16/19 and 15/18, not the printed 0.0013, 0.0665 and 0.1120 (the kappas inherit them, though all stay above 0.81); and Bartlett's df for 15 items is 105, not 1,050.
counterevidence_limits: Audits printed rounded numbers; Pc formula as P100 cites it (Polit et al.).
operationalization: APP Transcendence = auditing a scale validation
change_vs_prev_cycle: carried from TRA-APP-02 unchanged (not re-read in TRB)

wording: P103 developed an eight-week self-transcendence enhancement programme based on Reed's theory (body-scan meditation, life review, forgiveness, altruism and 'good death' sessions) for elderly Korean women living alone; among 34 completers (of 40) self-transcendence rose from 43.26 to 48.91 (t 8.78), spiritual well-being, positive affect and negative affect improved and depression fell (8.73 to 7.00), while life satisfaction did not change significantly.
locator: P103 Purpose to Conclusion, Tables 1-3 (read in full; supplementary data not read)
confidence: Low (single-group pre-post, 34 completers, no control group)
counterevidence_limits: No control group; maturation and confounding not controlled, as P103 states; facilitators also analysed the data. Slips: SPSS version 24.0 (abstract) vs 25.0 (methods); the four dimensions listed as 'individual, interpersonal, individual, and temporal'; 'increased ... negative affect' among the anticipated effects; see TRA-APP-04.
operationalization: APP Transcendence = a self-transcendence enhancement programme in nursing
verification_phrases: P103|the program was tested on a group of 40 elderly women aged 75 to 84 years living alone || P103|increased significantly from 43.26 points before participation in the program to 48.91 points || P103|but it was not statistically significant (t=1.72, p =.470)
change_vs_prev_cycle: carried from TRA-APP-03 unchanged (not re-read in TRB)

wording: Five of six pre-registered checks of P103 were not supported: life satisfaction's t 1.72 with 33 df gives one-tailed p 0.047, not the printed .470 (so it was in fact significant at the one-tailed .05 level used); pretest spiritual well-being is printed 56.52 although its subscales sum to 57.31 (posttest sums agree); discontinuation reasons add to 4, not 6; two of Table 2's percentages are off by more than rounding (26.6 for 9/34 = 26.5, 55.8 for 19/34 = 55.9); the Discussion's per-item affect means (3.37, 3.10) are not Table 3's posttest sums per item (3.56, 2.75). The a priori sample size of 32 reproduces. Printed p .002 for t 8.30 and 6.75 fall inside the 0.005 tolerance but the actual p values are below 1e-6.
counterevidence_limits: Audits printed rounded numbers; one-tailed p as P103 states.
operationalization: APP Transcendence = auditing an intervention study
change_vs_prev_cycle: carried from TRA-APP-04 unchanged (not re-read in TRB)

wording: Simulated chance agreement among 19 and 18 raters matches C(N, A) 0.5^N within 4 SE for every A tested, confirming the formula P100 cites; the correct Pc for 15 of 18 raters is 0.0031 (P100 prints 0.1120) and every corrected modified kappa for 15-19 of 19 agreeing raters stays at or above 0.78.
counterevidence_limits: Formula check; does not explain how P100 obtained its printed values.
operationalization: APP Transcendence = chance agreement in content validity
change_vs_prev_cycle: carried from TRA-APP-05 unchanged (not re-read in TRB)

wording: P103's printed means, SDs and t are mutually consistent (implied pre-post correlations 0.66 to 0.94; signs consistent), the paired effect size for self-transcendence is dz 1.51, and the design power at d .45 with the 34 completers is 0.82; at the observed effects power is near 1 except religious spiritual well-being and life satisfaction (about 0.54 and 0.52).
counterevidence_limits: Post hoc power at observed effects is descriptive only.
operationalization: APP Transcendence = consistency and power of an intervention study

wording: P100's universal-agreement S-CVI is 0.27 (4 of 15 items rated relevant by all 19 experts) against the reported average 0.92, so the 0.92 holds only on the averaging method; every item's I-CVI is at least 0.83. Modified kappa falls below 0.74 ('excellent') at 14 of 19 agreeing (0.73) and, with 6 raters, at 4 of 6 (0.56) but not 5 of 6 (0.82). P100's RMSEA reproduces with N or N - 1 alike.
counterevidence_limits: Thresholds as in Polit et al.; P100 does not report S-CVI/UA.
